object.acip: SOS KA'I DUS SU ZLA BA'I REG BYA'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, DE'I LUS SHES KYI MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I TSA BA'I REG BYA SKYE BA DANG , DGUN DUS SU NYI MA'I REG BYA'I CHA SHAS GCIG GIS NYER LEN DANG , YI DVAGS KYI LAS KYIS LHAN CIG BYED RKYEN BYAS PA LA BRTEN NAS, DE'I LUS SHES KYI MYONG BYAR GYUR PA'I GRANG BA'I REG BYA SKYE BA YOD PA LTA BU YIN PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: sos ka'i dus su zla ba'i reg bya'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas, de'i lus shes kyi myong byar gyur pa'i tsha ba'i reg bya skye ba dang , dgun dus su nyi ma'i reg bya'i cha shas gcig gis nyer len dang , yi dvags kyi las kyis lhan cig byed rkyen byas pa la brten nas, de'i lus shes kyi myong byar gyur pa'i grang ba'i reg bya skye ba yod pa lta bu yin pa'i phyir
object.english: Another example would be the moon in springtime; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of a craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of heat, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body. So too with the wintertime sun; one part of the feel of its rays on the body provides the material cause, and then the karma of the craving spirit provides a contributing factor. Based on these two, the spirit gets a sensation of cold, which is experienced by the consciousness of the body.

object.acip: DE LTAR SKYE BA YIN TE, BSHES SPRING LAS, YI DVAGS RNAMS LA SOS KA'I DUS SU NI, , ZLA BA'ANG TSA LA DGUN NI NYI MA'ANG GRANG , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: de ltar skye ba yin te, bshes spring las, yi dvags rnams la sos ka'i dus su ni, , zla ba'ang tsha la dgun ni nyi ma'ang grang , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
object.english: It is a fact that they get this kind of sensation, for [Arya Nagarjuna's] Letter to a Friend states: For craving spirits, even the light of the moon In the spring is hot, and even the winter sun cold.

object.acip: DE YANG YUL DUS KHYAD PAR CAN DE DAG GI DBANG GIS SKYE BA YIN GYI SPYIR DE LTAR SKYE BA MA YIN TE, NYI MA'I STENG DU GRANG BA'I REG BYA YANG MED, ZLA BA'I STENG DU TSA BA'I REG BYA YANG MED PA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, NYI MA'I STENG DU MUN PA'I RDZAS MED PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: de yang yul dus khyad par can de dag gi dbang gis skye ba yin gyi spyir de ltar skye ba ma yin te, nyi ma'i steng du grang ba'i reg bya yang med, zla ba'i steng du tsha ba'i reg bya yang med pa'i phyir, der thal, nyi ma'i steng du mun pa'i rdzas med pa'i phyir
object.english: All of this is caused by the extraordinary circumstances of the particular time and place, for generally speaking it never happens this way: there is nothing at all about the sun that can feel cold, and nothing about the moon that can feel hot. This too is a fact, for there does not exist on the sun any case of that substance we call "covered space."

object.acip: GSUM PA DE LA RTZOD PA SPONG BA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG PO LA, LAS CAN GYI 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG PO DE, CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN GYI CHA CAN DU SKYES KYANG , 'GRO BA GSUM PO DES RANG RANG GI THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I LAS KYI DBANG GIS, 'GRO BA RE RES DNGOS PO GSUM GA MA MTHONG BAR KHAS BLANGS PA LA,
object.wylie: gsum pa de la rtsod pa spong ba la, brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po la, las can gyi 'gro ba gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de, cha shas gsum ldan gyi cha can du skyes kyang , 'gro ba gsum po des rang rang gi thun mong ma yin pa'i las kyi dbang gis, 'gro ba re res dngos po gsum ga ma mthong bar khas blangs pa la
object.english: Here is the third part of our presentation, where we refute the rebuttal of representatives of other views. You will recall that our own position is describing a situation where beings of three different types, each with their own karma, are sitting together and looking at a glass filled with something that is wet and flowing. The glass filled with something wet and flowing exists, at this point, as something with three distinct parts. Nonetheless, no one of the beings is able to see all three things there, for they are each at the mercy of the particular karma that they themselves have collected. Representatives of other viewpoints now come to attack this position.

object.acip: KHA CIG, DE LTAR 'DOD PA DE MI 'THAD PAR THAL, DPAL LDAN CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DANG 'GAL BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, DE'I GZHUNG LAS, GAL TE DE YANG MTHONG MED LA, , BRTEN NAS GZUGS GZHAN 'BYUNG 'GYUR NA, , ZHES DGRA GNYEN GNYIS KYIS SKYES BU GCIG GI GZUGS LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, SKYES BU DE'I GZUGS MDZES MI MDZES GNYIS SU GNAS KYANG , GZUGS DE DANG DGRA GNYEN GNYIS KYI BAR DU LAS GZUGS SKYES PAS, DGRA GNYEN GNYIS PO DES GZUGS MDZES MI MDZES GNYIS KA MA MTHONG BA, GRANGS CAN GYIS KHAS BLANGS PA DE 'GOG BYED KYI RIGS PA KHA SPOS PAS KHYOD KYI DE LA GNOD PA'I PHYIR ZER NA,
object.wylie: kha cig, de ltar 'dod pa de mi 'thad par thal, dpal ldan chos kyi grags pa'i lung dang 'gal ba'i phyir, der thal, de'i gzhung las, gal te de yang mthong med la, , brten nas gzugs gzhan 'byung 'gyur na, , zhes dgra gnyen gnyis kyis skyes bu gcig gi gzugs la bltas pa de'i tshe na, skyes bu de'i gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis su gnas kyang , gzugs de dang dgra gnyen gnyis kyi bar du las gzugs skyes pas, dgra gnyen gnyis po des gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis ka ma mthong ba, grangs can gyis khas blangs pa de 'gog byed kyi rigs pa kha spos pas khyod kyi de la gnod pa'i phyir zer na
object.english: One comes and makes the following claim: Your position, as just explained, is mistaken, for it goes against a statement of the glorious Dharmakirti. This is quite surely the case, for in his major work [entitled The Commentary on Valid Perception] he says, Suppose you say that they don't see it, And circumstances cause another form. What he's talking about here is a belief of the [non- Buddhist] Numerist School. They give the case of a single person whose physical form is looked upon at the same time by his enemy, and also by his friend. In reality, the person's physical form is both attractive and ugly at the same time. Something happens where yet another physical form, one from karma, grows up between the person's true physical form and the enemy and friend looking at it. Because of this neither the enemy nor the friend sees both the attractiveness and the ugliness together. Master Dharmakirti uses logic to refute this concept, and this same logic can be used against the position you have taken, to prove that you are wrong.

object.acip: DE MI 'THAD PAR THAL, DE LTAR 'DOD PA DE NI CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DON DANG , PHYOGS SNGA SMRA BA PO'I 'DOD PA GNYIS KA KHONG DU MA CHUD PA'I SKYON YIN PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: de mi 'thad par thal, de ltar 'dod pa de ni chos kyi grags pa'i lung don dang , phyogs snga smra ba po'i 'dod pa gnyis ka khong du ma chud pa'i skyon yin pa'i phyir
object.english: Your reasoning here is though incorrect, for the belief you have expressed shows that you have failed to understand both the meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement, and the whole position expressed above.

object.acip: DER THAL, CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DON NI, GRANGS CAN GYIS RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS DANG , MIG SHES GNYIS KYI BAR DU, LAS GZUGS GSAL MI GSAL SKYE BA'I DBANG GIS, GZUGS GSAL BAR SNANG MI SNANG 'JOG PA YIN GYI, GZUGS KYI RNAM PA SHAR BA'I SGO NAS GZUGS GSAL BAR SNANG MI SNANG 'JOG PA MA YIN ZHES KHAS BLANGS PA LA, DE LTA BU'I LAS GZUGS GNYIS PO DES RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS GNYIS PO DE BSGRIBS SAM MA BSGRIBS, BSGRIBS NA MIG SHES KYIS GZUGS GNYIS PO DE MA MTHONG BAR THAL, DES DE SGRIB PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: der thal, chos kyi grags pa'i lung don ni, grangs can gyis rgyang ring thung gi gzugs la bltas pa de'i tshe na, rgyang ring thung gi gzugs dang , mig shes gnyis kyi bar du, las gzugs gsal mi gsal skye ba'i dbang gis, gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa yin gyi, gzugs kyi rnam pa shar ba'i sgo nas gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa ma yin zhes khas blangs pa la, de lta bu'i las gzugs gnyis po des rgyang ring thung gi gzugs gnyis po de bsgribs sam ma bsgribs, bsgribs na mig shes kyis gzugs gnyis po de ma mthong bar thal, des de sgrib pa'i phyir
object.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this form. In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

object.acip: MA BSGRIBS NA, MIG SHES DES LAS GZUGS GNYIS DANG RGYANG RING THUNG GI GZUGS GNYIS PO DE CIG CAR DU MTHONG BAR THAL, DES DE MA BSGRIBS PA'I PHYIR ZHES BKAG PA'I DON YIN PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: ma bsgribs na, mig shes des las gzugs gnyis dang rgyang ring thung gi gzugs gnyis po de cig car du mthong bar thal, des de ma bsgribs pa'i phyir zhes bkag pa'i don yin pa'i phyir
object.english: And suppose you say that they do not obscure them. Wouldn't your visual consciousness then see both the two intermediate forms created by karma, and the two original forms, the near one and the far one, all at the same time? They would have to because, according to you, the intermediate forms do not obscure the original ones. This is the real point of the Master's statement, wherein he refutes that belief of the Numerists.

object.acip: GNYIS PA DER THAL, PHYOGS SNGA MAS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG PO DE, DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN DU YANG KHAS MA BLANGS, SKYES BU GCIG GI GZUGS MDZES MI MDZES GNYIS KA YIN PAR YANG KHAS MA BLANGS, YI DVAGS KYIS MIG SHES DANG CHU KLUNG GI BAR DU RNAG KHRAG GI LAS GZUGS SKYE BAR KHAS MA BLANGS, YI DVAGS KYI MIG GIS RNAG KHRAG GI LAS GZUGS DANG CHU KLUNG GNYIS KA MTHONG BAR YANG KHAS MA BLANGS, LAS KYI DBANG GIS YI DVAGS KYI CHU KLUNG MA MTHONG BAR KHAS BLANGS PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: gnyis pa der thal, phyogs snga mas brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la, 'gro ba gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de, dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun du yang khas ma blangs, skyes bu gcig gi gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis ka yin par yang khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyis mig shes dang chu klung gi bar du rnag khrag gi las gzugs skye bar khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyi mig gis rnag khrag gi las gzugs dang chu klung gnyis ka mthong bar yang khas ma blangs, las kyi dbang gis yi dvags kyi chu klung ma mthong bar khas blangs pa'i phyir
object.english: Our second point [that you have failed to comprehend the position we expressed above] is also quite true. Our original position was describing a situation where three different kinds of beings were sitting together and looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It is not our position that the glass full of something wet and flowing is one thing that is three different things. And it is not our position that there is such a thing as the physical appearance of a person which is at once both attractive and ugly. It is furthermore not our position that the blood and pus represent some kind of physical form which results from karma and grows up between the visual consciousness of the craving spirit and the stream of water. And it is not our position that the craving spirit's eyes see both this blood and pus as some kind of physical form resulting from karma, and the river of water at the same time. It is our position that, by force of his karma, the craving spirit is not able to see the stream of water.

object.acip: GZHAN YANG , DPAL CHOS KYI GRAGS PA'I LUNG DANG KHYOD 'GAL BA YIN TE, KHYOD KYI NAD LNGA DANG , 'BYUNG BA LNGA DANG , GDON LNGA DANG BCAS PA RNAMS, NYON MONGS PA DUG LNGA'I DNGOS 'BRAS SU KHAS BLANGS, MU STEGS BYED KYI BAD KAN DANG 'DOD CHAGS RGYU 'BRAS, MKHRIS PA DANG ZHE SDANG RGYU 'BRAS SOGS SU KHAS BLANGS PA LA, BAD KAN DANG 'DOD CHAGS RJES SU 'GRO LDOG 'KHRUL, MKHRIS PA DANG ZHE SDANG RJES SU 'GRO LDOG 'KHRUL PAS DE 'GOG BYED KYI, 'KHRUL PHYIR RLUNG SOGS CHOS MA YIN, , ZHES PA'I GZHUNG 'DON PA SGYUR BA'I SGO NAS KHYOD LA GNOD PA'I PHYIR DANG , 'DUS MA BYAS KYI NAM MKHA' PHRAG DOG GI DNGOS 'BRAS SU 'DOD PA MI RIGS PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: gzhan yang , dpal chos kyi grags pa'i lung dang khyod 'gal ba yin te, khyod kyi nad lnga dang , 'byung ba lnga dang , gdon lnga dang bcas pa rnams, nyon mongs pa dug lnga'i dngos 'bras su khas blangs, mu stegs byed kyi bad kan dang 'dod chags rgyu 'bras, mkhris pa dang zhe sdang rgyu 'bras sogs su khas blangs pa la, bad kan dang 'dod chags rjes su 'gro ldog 'khrul, mkhris pa dang zhe sdang rjes su 'gro ldog 'khrul pas de 'gog byed kyi, 'khrul phyir rlung sogs chos ma yin, , zhes pa'i gzhung 'don pa sgyur ba'i sgo nas khyod la gnod pa'i phyir dang , 'dus ma byas kyi nam mkha' phrag dog gi dngos 'bras su 'dod pa mi rigs pa'i phyir
object.english: And anyway, maybe it's you who have contradicted a statement of the glorious Dharmakirti. You have taken the position that the five sicknesses, and the five elements, and the five demons are all the direct result of the five poisons--the five bad thoughts. But when the non-Buddhists take the position that phlegm and desire have a cause-and-effect relationship, and that bile and anger have the same kind of relationship, and so on, then Master Dharmakirti refutes them by showing that desire doesn't always come and go according to the phlegm, and anger doesn't always come and go according to the bile. To do so he makes the statement that says, "It's not a fact that wind and the rest are such, for the relationship doesn't always hold." We could twist around this statement too and say that it disproved your position; and add as well how wrong it is to assert that uncreated space could ever be the direct result of jealousy. [The point seems to be that, although your position about the bad thoughts, and our original position on the nature of the three beings' perceptions, are both correct, you could always twist around some quotation by a master, take it out of context or misinterpret it, and try to show they were wrong.]

object.acip: YANG KHA CIG NA RE, DNGOS GCIG YID NI THA DAD PHYIR, , DON MA GRUB PAR 'DOD PA YIN, , ZHES DNGOS PO GCIG LA SNANG TSUL MI 'DRA BA GSUM 'BYUNG BAR GSUNGS PA MI 'THAD PAR THAL, KHYOD LTAR NA DNGOS PO GSUM LA SNANG TSUL MI 'DRA BA GSUM 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR, DER THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, DNGOS PO TSAD GRUB PA GSUM LA SNANG TSUL MI 'DRA BA GSUM 'BYUNG BA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,

object.english: Someone else might come and make yet another claim: Let's talk about that quotation above, where it said: Insofar as [these different beings] have differing perceptions Of a single thing, we say it has no reality. The idea being expressed here is that a single object can be appearing in three different ways. This is incorrect because, according to you, what's happening is that three different objects are appearing in three different ways. And this certainly is your position; remember, you were describing a situation where three different kinds of beings sit down together and look at a glass full of something that's wet and flowing. You said that there were three different objects, each confirmed by a valid perception, and that they were appearing in three different ways.

object.acip: 'O NA, SKYES BU GCIG GIS YAN LAG MI 'DRA BA LNGAS BYA BA MI 'DRA BA LNGA BYAS PA DE'I TSE NA, SKYES BU GCIG GIS BYA BA MI 'DRA BA LNGA BYAS PA MA YIN PAR THAL, YAN LAG MI 'DRA BA LNGAS BYA BA MI 'DRA BA LNGA BYAS PA'I PHYIR,

object.english: Well now, suppose a person is using all four of his limbs, and his head, to perform five different actions. According to you, it wouldn't be one person performing five different actions, because five different protuberances of his body are performing five different actions.

object.acip: BYAS PA LA KHO NA RE, SKYON MED DE, YAN LAG LNGA PO DE SKYES BU DE'I CHA SHAS YIN PAS, DES BYA BA BYAS PAS SKYES BU DES BYA BA BYAS PAR 'JOG DGOS PA'I PHYIR, ZER NA,

object.english: In response to this line of reasoning, someone responds: No, there's no such problem here. The five protuberances are all parts of the one person, so we have to say that, when the five are performing some actions, the person is performing some actions.

object.english: Well the case above is exactly the same! The three things mentioned, the blood and pus and the other two, are all parts of the glass full of something wet and flowing. When the three appear then we can say that the glass full of a thing which is wet and flowing is acting as a basis, and that three different ways of appearing are being displayed upon it.

object.wylie: der thal chos kyi grags pa'i lung don ni grangs can gyis rgyang ring thung gi, gzugs la bltas pa de'i tshe na rgyang ring thung gi gzugs dang mig shes gnyis kyi bar du las gzugs gsal mi gsal skye ba'i dbang gis gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa yin gyi gzugs kyi rnam pa shar ba'i sgo nas gzugs gsal bar snang mi snang 'jog pa ma yin zhes khas blangs pa la de lta bu'i las gzugs gnyis po des rgyang ring thung gi gzugs gnyis po de bsgribs sam ma bsgribs bsgribs na mig shes kyis gzugs gnyis po de ma mthong bar thal des de sgrib pa'i phyir
object.english: This is a fact, for the actual meaning of Master Dharmakirti's statement is as follows. The Numerist School is describing a situation where you are looking at a physical form either from far away, or from up close. They say that, depending on the distance between you and the object, another physical form which is the result of karma, and which stands between your visual consciousness and the original form, is either clear or not. This then determines whether the original form appears to you distinctly or not. It is not the case though, they say, that what determines whether the original form appears clearly or not is whether or not you have a clear impression of this In reply then Master Dharmakirti is asking the Numerists: Let's consider these two cases of some intermediate physical form that comes from karma. Do they, or do they not, function to obscure the two original forms, the one at a distance, and the other close by? If they were to obscure them, then your visual consciousness could never see the two original forms, since they would have been obscured by the others.

object.acip: `GNYIS PA RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LAS CAN GYI LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN PA MA YIN PA DANG , DE'I TSE TSAD MTSUNGS GSUM NGES PAR MI DGOS SHING , BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU SKYE BA DANG ,
object.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
object.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.

object.acip: DNGOS PO GSUM PHAN TSUN GO SA 'GOG PA'I DNGOS PO MA YIN PAR THAL BA'I RIGS PAS MI GNOD DE, DE'I TSE NA BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG PO DE, DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN DU YANG KHAS MA BLANGS, TSAD MTSUNGS NGES PAR DGOS PAR YANG KHAS MA BLANGS PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: dngos po gsum phan tshun go sa 'gog pa'i dngos po ma yin par thal ba'i rigs pas mi gnod de, de'i tshe na brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de, dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun du yang khas ma blangs, tshad mtshungs nges par dgos par yang khas ma blangs pa'i phyir
object.english: This kind of reasoning, where you attempt to show that we are implying that the three objects are not the kinds that block each other from entering the space that each one occupies, cannot disprove our position. Neither did we ever say that there definitely had to be identical valid perceptions here.

object.wylie: gnyis pa der thal, phyogs snga mas brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la, 'gro ba gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang po de, dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun du yang khas ma blangs, skyes bu gcig gi gzugs mdzes mi mdzes gnyis ka yin par yang khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyis mig shes dang chu klung gi bar du rnag khrag gi las gzugs skye bar khas ma blangs, yi dvags kyi mig gis rnag khrag gi las gzugs dang chu klung gnyis ka mthong bar yang khas ma blangs, las kyi dbang gis yi dvags kyi chu klung ma mthong bar khas blangs pa'i phyir
object.english: Our second point [that you have failed to comprehend the position we expressed above] is also quite true. It is our position that, by force of his karma, the craving spirit is not able to see the stream of water.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, NGAR 'DZIN LHAN SKYES KYIS BZUNG BA LTAR GRUB PA'I BDAG DE CHOS CAN, PHUNG PO'I STENG DU MED DE, PHUNG PO'I STENG DU DE DANG GCIG DANG DU MA GANG RUNG DU MA GRUB PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, ngar 'dzin lhan skyes kyis bzung ba ltar grub pa'i bdag de chos can, phung po'i steng du med de, phung po'i steng du de dang gcig dang du ma gang rung du ma grub pa'i phyir
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: a second way of looking at the subject under consideration here. Let's consider a “me” which could actually exist in the way that our automatic tendency to grasp to a “me” holds it to be. No such thing exists relative to the parts of me; Because it exists neither as one thing relative to these parts, nor as more than one thing relative to these parts.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, MYU GU CHOS CAN, GZHAN LAS MI SKYE STE, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RGYU GZHAN LAS MI SKYE BA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, myu gu chos can, gzhan las mi skye ste, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i rgyu gzhan las mi skye ba'i phyir
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: Consider a sprout. It cannot start from something other than itself; Because it cannot start from a cause other than itself which exists by definition.

object.acip: GNYIS PA ZHI GNAS SGRUB TSUL DNGOS NI, DBUS MTHA' LAS, ,NYES PA LNGA SPONG 'DU BYED BRGYAD, ,BSTEN PA'I RGYU LAS BYUNG BA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa zhi gnas sgrub tshul dngos ni, dbus mtha' las, ,nyes pa lnga spong 'du byed brgyad, ,bsten pa'i rgyu las byung ba'o
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: the actual method for developing quietude. Distinguishing the Middle from the Extremes says that: The cause that will bring it to you Is avoiding five different problems, And making use of eight Different kinds of action. The five classic problems that come up during meditation

object.acip: ,,GNYIS PA SO SOR BSHAD PA LA BZHI, BYE BRAG SMRA BA, MDO SDE PA, SEMS TZAM PA, DBU MA PA'I GRUB MTHA' 'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa so sor bshad pa la bzhi, bye brag smra ba, mdo sde pa, sems tsam pa, dbu ma pa'i grub mtha' 'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point promised above, which is a separate explanation of each of the four inner systems.  We proceed, naturally, through four sections, covering the belief systems of the Detailists; the Sutrists; the Mind Only; and the Middle Way.

object.acip: ,,GNYIS PA LAM LA GNYIS TE, SPANG BYA NI BYE SMRA DANG MTHUN CING LAM GYI DMIGS PA NI BDEN BZHI'I RNAM PA MI RTAG LA SOGS BCU DRUG PO NYID YIN LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa lam la gnyis te, spang bya ni bye smra dang mthun cing lam gyi dmigs pa ni bden bzhi'i rnam pa mi rtag la sogs bcu drug po nyid yin la
object.english: We will cover our second point here—on how the Sutrist system describes the path—in two parts.  As for the things within us that we must eliminate by following this path, their beliefs are in accordance with those of the Detailists.  As for the subjects that the path focuses upon, they are those same 16 aspects of the four higher truths: impermanence and the rest.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, RTAG CHAD KYI MTHA' DANG BRAL BA'I DNGOS PO BDEN MED DU RTOGS PA'I LTA BA KHAS LEN PAS NA, DBU MA PA DANG,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, rtag chad kyi mtha' dang bral ba'i dngos po bden med du rtogs pa'i lta ba khas len pas na, dbu ma pa dang
object.english: As for our second point—the literal meaning of the name “Middle Way”—those who adhere to this system are referred to as “practitioners of the Middle Way” because they accept a viewpoint in which we finally realize that there is no entity in the universe which exists in truth—and thus free ourselves forever from the two extremes of things having to exist forever, or things suddenly stopping altogether.

object.acip: ,GNYIS PA LAM LA GNYIS, LAM GYI SPANG BYA DANG, LAM GYI RNAM GZHAG DNGOS SU {%SO,}
object.wylie: gnyis pa lam la gnyis, lam gyi spang bya dang, lam gyi rnam gzhag dngos su {%so,}
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, which is how the Independent branch describes the path to correct our original condition.  We proceed in two steps: a description of undesirable objects which the path eliminates, and then the actual presentation of the path itself.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LAM DNGOS LA, THEG PA GSUM RANG RANG GI LAM LA TSOGS LAM SOGS LNGA RE YOD LA, MDO SDE SPYOD PA'I DBU MA PA LTAR NA, NYAN RANG GNYIS KAS GTZO BOR NYON SGRIB SPONG BAR MTSUNGS SHING, THOB BYA LA YANG MCHOG DMAN CHER MED KYANG,
object.wylie: gnyis pa lam dngos la, theg pa gsum rang rang gi lam la tshogs lam sogs lnga re yod la, mdo sde spyod pa'i dbu ma pa ltar na, nyan rang gnyis kas gtso bor nyon sgrib spong bar mtshungs shing, thob bya la yang mchog dman cher med kyang
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, on the actual path itself.  Members of the Independent branch of the Middle Way would say that each overall path through each of the three tracks consists itself of five paths, starting with the path of accumulation.  Those of the Independent branch who lean towards the Sutrist system would say that listeners and self-made buddhas are equivalent in the sense that they are, primarily, working to eliminate obstacles to nirvana.  And they would say that there are no great degrees of higher or lower between these two tracks.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, THAL 'GYUR GYI SGO NAS PHYI RGOL GYI RGYUD LA BSGRUB BYA RTOGS PA'I RJES DPAG SKYE BAR 'DOD PA'I DBU MA PA YIN PAS NA, DBU MA THAL 'GYUR BA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, thal 'gyur gyi sgo nas phyi rgol gyi rgyud la bsgrub bya rtogs pa'i rjes dpag skye bar 'dod pa'i dbu ma pa yin pas na, dbu ma thal 'gyur ba'o
object.english: Here is our second point.  The word “Consequence” in the name of this branch of the Middle Way is meant to indicate the members of this group are followers of the Middle Way who believe that one can—through the use of a logical statement which points up the absurd consequences of an opponent's position—inspire in that opponent a deductive form of accurate perception which confirms the point we are trying to prove to them. The original condition, according to the Consequence branch within the Middle Way system

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, NANG SDE GNAS MA BU PAS, GANG ZAG RTAG GCIG RANG DBANG CAN GYI KHYAD PAR GSUM PO DES STONG PA GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED PHRA MOR 'DOD LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, nang sde gnas ma bu pas, gang zag rtag gcig rang dbang can gyi khyad par gsum po des stong pa gang zag gi bdag med phra mor 'dod la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: what it means when we say that something is empty of existing in a self-standing, substantial way.  Now the inner belief system of the followers of Vatsiputra describes the subtle lack of a self-nature to the person as the person's emptiness of three different details: existing in an unchanging way; existing as something singular; and existing as something which is independent.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LAM LA GNYIS, SPYIR BSTAN PA DANG, PHYE BA SO SOR BSHAD PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa lam la gnyis, spyir bstan pa dang, phye ba so sor bshad pa'o
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: the actual presentation of the path in this second branch.  We proceed in two steps: a general presentation, followed by an explanation of each of the separate components.

object.acip: [E73] GNYIS PA NI, DE LTAR NA SANGS RGYAS DANG SLOB MA NYAN THOS RNAMS LA THUN MONG DU YOD PA KUN SHES PA NYID KYI LAM GYI RTEN CAN GYI RNAM PA SUM CU RTZA BDUN NO,,
object.wylie: [e73] gnyis pa ni, de ltar na sangs rgyas dang slob ma nyan thos rnams la thun mong du yod pa kun shes pa nyid kyi lam gyi rten can gyi rnam pa sum cu rtsa bdun no
object.english: Which brings us finally to our second point: a summary of the general import.  Given the above explanations, we can say then that there are 37 different aspects that revolve around that “one knowledge about things” and which are shared by the Enlightened Ones with “students,” or listeners. Part Two: 34 aspects of path knowledge shared with the bodhisattvas

object.acip: [E139] GNYIS PA NI, DE LTAR NA SOGS SO,,
object.wylie: [e139] gnyis pa ni, de ltar na sogs so
object.english: As for our second point here—a summary of the 34 aspects of enlightenment shared with the bodhisattvas—refer to the section that mentions “as such.” Part Three: 39 aspects possessed only by a fully Enlightened Being

object.acip: [E142] GNYIS PA LA BRTEN PA YON TAN DANG, RTEN YE SHES SO,,
object.wylie: [e142] gnyis pa la brten pa yon tan dang, rten ye shes so
object.english: Which brings us to our second point: the expanded explanation.  Here we will first describe that which does the relying—the fine qualities; and then what they rely upon—wisdom.

object.acip: [E171] ,GNYIS PA RTEN YE SHES LA GSUM LAS, JI LTA BA MKHYEN PA'I YE SHES NI,
object.wylie: [e171] ,gnyis pa rten ye shes la gsum las, ji lta ba mkhyen pa'i ye shes ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point: the wisdom that those fine qualities rely upon.  Here there are three divisions; we begin with the wisdom which knows the way all things are.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, GZHAN YANG SA DANG PO LA GNAS PA 'DI NI SO SKYE DANG NYAN RANG GI SA THAMS CAD LAS 'DAS PA'I PHYIR DANG, SANGS RGYAS KYI SA'I RJES SU 'GRO BAR NGES PA'I LAM RGYUD LA SKYES PA'I PHYIR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS KYI RIGS SU'ANG SKYES PA STE, LAM GZHAN DU MI 'GRO BAR RANG GI LAM DU RIGS NGES PA YIN NO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gzhan yang sa dang po la gnas pa 'di ni so skye dang nyan rang gi sa thams cad las 'das pa'i phyir dang, sangs rgyas kyi sa'i rjes su 'gro bar nges pa'i lam rgyud la skyes pa'i phyir de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi rigs su'ang skyes pa ste, lam gzhan du mi 'gro bar rang gi lam du rigs nges pa yin no
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: the high quality with the four characteristics which begin with taking birth into a royal family. We can moreover add that this person who is at the first bodhisattva level has taken birth into the family of Those Gone Thus—because they have gone far beyond the levels of common beings, and both the listeners & self made buddhas; and moreover because they have now given rise, within their hearts, to a path which is definite to lead them to the level of a Buddha. That is, they are confirmed within the family of their own path, and will never go off to some different path.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, TSUL KHRIMS DANG BRAL NA SBYIN 'BRAS NGAN 'GRO'I RTEN LA SMIN PA DANG, RTEN DE LA SNGAR GYI SBYIN PA'I 'BRAS BU LONGS SPYOD PA TZAM YIN GYI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, tshul khrims dang bral na sbyin 'bras ngan 'gro'i rten la smin pa dang, rten de la sngar gyi sbyin pa'i 'bras bu longs spyod pa tsam yin gyi
object.english: Here next is our second point from above: how enjoying the fruits of these acts of giving in a succession of lifetimes depends upon continuing to follow an ethical way of life. If we fail to follow an ethical life, then the fruits of our giving will come back to us as we live in the body & mind of a being in the lower realms; and in this body & mind we will enjoy nothing more than the wealth which results from the giving we did in our former body & mind.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, YANG CI'I PHYIR SA 'DI LA 'OD 'PHRO BA ZHES BRJOD CE NA, SA BZHI PA DER NI BDE BAR GSHEGS PA'I SRAS PO LA, RDZOGS PA YI BYANG CHUB KYI PHYOGS KYI CHOS SO BDUN, SNGAR LAS LHAG PAR BSGOMS PA LAS SKYES PA'I YE SHES KYI SNANG BA, SA GSUM PAR BSHAD PA'I ZANGS KYI 'OD DANG 'DRA BA LAS LHAG PA 'BYUNG STE, DE'I PHYIR YANG DAG PA'I YE SHES KYI ME'I 'OD LHAG PA 'BYUNG BAS, BYANG SEMS KYI SA DE LA 'OD 'PHRO BA ZHES BYA STE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, yang ci'i phyir sa 'di la 'od 'phro ba zhes brjod ce na, sa bzhi pa der ni bde bar gshegs pa'i sras po la, rdzogs pa yi byang chub kyi phyogs kyi chos so bdun, sngar las lhag par bsgoms pa las skyes pa'i ye shes kyi snang ba, sa gsum par bshad pa'i zangs kyi 'od dang 'dra ba las lhag pa 'byung ste, de'i phyir yang dag pa'i ye shes kyi me'i 'od lhag pa 'byung bas, byang sems kyi sa de la 'od 'phro ba zhes bya ste
object.english: Which brings us to our second point—the reason for the name. Now you may ask, again, why this level is given the name it is: Radiance. It is because here, at the fourth level, the children of Those Gone to Bliss practice the 37 qualities of perfect enlightenment to a degree which is even higher than ever before. And then a light arises from this practice—an exceeding light of wisdom is born, similar to the copper-colored light we spoke of for the third level. And so because at this bodhisattva level there shines this higher light of pure wisdom, we give it the name of “Radiance.”

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, BLO'I DBANG GIS BZHAG PA DANG MA BZHAG PA'I YOD PA JI LTAR YIN SHES PA LA, SGYU MA'I DPE'I STENG NAS SHES PAR BYED PA BSNGAGS PAS DE BSHAD NA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, blo'i dbang gis bzhag pa dang ma bzhag pa'i yod pa ji ltar yin shes pa la, sgyu ma'i dpe'i steng nas shes par byed pa bsngags pas de bshad na
object.english: Here then is our second point from above: a presentation of the metaphor of a magician, to demonstrate from a worldly point of view the difference between what is real and what is false. One may begin by asking: “What do you mean when you say that something is, or isn't, 'established by the mind'?” A method where we learn this point through the metaphor of a magic show is highly recommended; and so we will present it here.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, SKYON SPONG GI LAN, LAN DE DGAG PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, skyon spong gi lan, lan de dgag pa'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: denying a response which attempts to avoid the problem. We proceed in two steps: a presentation of this response, and then denying it.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: refuting attempted rebuttal of our denial.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: a description of other ways in which the two realities are set forth.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of this unique presentation on the negative emotions.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Here is our second point from above, which is how the simple deception either makes its appearance, or does not make its appearance, to three different types of individuals.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, RTZA BA'I TSIG DON BSHAD PA DANG, DE LA RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, rtsa ba'i tshig don bshad pa dang, de la rtsod pa spang ba'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of that reality which is ultimate. We proceed in two steps: an explanation of the words of the root text at this point, and then a refutation of argument concerning their meaning. Here is the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This then brings us to our second point from above: refuting rebuttal upon the points we've made.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above, where we deny the belief that things could exist by definition, through demonstrating that it would have to be the case that nominal reality could stand up under logical analysis.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from before: disproving any argument against our denial that things could exist by definition.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MI 'DOD PA LA KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS BLANG MI DGOS PAR BSTAN PA DANG, LAS 'GAGS PA LAS 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BA'I DPE BSTAN PA DANG, DE LTAR BSTAN PA LA RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, rang bzhin gyis grub pa mi 'dod pa la kun gzhi sogs khas blang mi dgos par bstan pa dang, las 'gags pa las 'bras bu 'byung ba'i dpe bstan pa dang, de ltar bstan pa la rtsod pa spang ba'o
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: The advantage of showing that the connection between karma and its consequences is eminently correct. Here we proceed in three steps: a demonstration that it is not the case that if we deny that things could exist through any nature of their own, we must then accept things like foundation consciousness; the presentation of a metaphor to illustrate how a karmic consequence can come from the karma itself having stopped; and then finally disproving any debate that may arise about this presentation.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: how it is that the metaphor of a dream fails to establish the idea that, when we awake, there are no outer objects.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: showing how other such sutras should be taken figuratively as well.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: showing how logic takes these statements as figurative.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, DE'I DON BSDUS TE BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, dngos kyi don dang, de'i don bsdus te bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from before: refuting debate about this denial. We proceed in two sections: the actual point, and a summary presentation. Here is the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: Refuting the answer, where the other side attempts to deny the problems we've raised.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Here then is our second point from before: a presentation of support for saying that the kind of belief presented is incorrect.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: denying the position that the outline itself could be the wagon.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: With this we have reached our second point from above: denying that what belongs to the self could exist through any nature of its own.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, which is how it is that we accept the proof of our own position.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: an incidental presentation on how we accept a nature to things.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: With this we have reached our second point from above: an explanation of the remaining three types of emptiness here. 2) Emptiness on the outside

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of the four types of emptiness starting with great emptiness. 5) Great emptiness

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: the own quality of things related to the time of the path.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DE KHO NA NYID RTOGS PA MI 'THAD PA'I RTZOD PA SPANG BA, MKHYEN PA PO MI 'THAD PA'I RTZOD PA SPANG BA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, de kho na nyid rtogs pa mi 'thad pa'i rtsod pa spang ba, mkhyen pa po mi 'thad pa'i rtsod pa spang ba'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: our actual refutation of argument on the way in which we first reach our enlightenment. Here we proceed in two steps: refuting argument which says that the idea of realizing suchness is mistaken; and then refuting argument which says that our idea about the one who gains the knowledge in this case is mistaken as well. [afterword.13] Sanskrit unavailable

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DNGOS KYI DON DANG, DE'I 'THAD PA DNGOS BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, dngos kyi don dang, de'i 'thad pa dngos bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: With this we have come to our second point from above: refuting argument which says that our idea about the one who gains the knowledge in this case is mistaken as well. This we present in two sections: the actual point, and then a direct demonstration of how it is correct. Here is the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, SKU'I RNAM GZHAG DANG, STOBS KYI YON TAN GYI RNAM GZHAG GO
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, sku'i rnam gzhag dang, stobs kyi yon tan gyi rnam gzhag go
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: a description of the holy body, and the fine qualities, that we then achieve. We proceed in two sections: a presentation of the holy bodies; and then a description of the fine qualities of the forces.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of the holy body complete in all enjoyments.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: the way in which these beings display all the activities of others in that same location. [afterword.23] Sanskrit unavailable

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA BZHI, STOBS BCU MDOR BSTAN PA{%,} DE RNAMS RGYAS PAR BSHAD, YON TAN KUN BRJOD MI NUS PA'I TSUL, YON TAN GNYIS SHES PA'I PHAN YON BSTAN PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la bzhi, stobs bcu mdor bstan pa{%,} de rnams rgyas par bshad, yon tan kun brjod mi nus pa'i tshul, yon tan gnyis shes pa'i phan yon bstan pa'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from before—a description of the fine qualities of the forces. Here we cover four topics: a brief presentation of the ten forces; a more extensive explanation of the same; a discussion of how it would be impossible ever to describe all these fine qualities; and a demonstration of the benefits of understanding the two kinds of fine qualities. Here is the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, GNAS DANG GNAS MIN MKHYEN PA SOGS KYI STOBS LNGA BSHAD PA DANG, THAMS CAD DU 'GRO BA'I LAM MKHYEN PA SOGS KYI STOBS LNGA BSHAD PA'O, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, gnas dang gnas min mkhyen pa sogs kyi stobs lnga bshad pa dang, thams cad du 'gro ba'i lam mkhyen pa sogs kyi stobs lnga bshad pa'o, ,dang po ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: more extensive explanation of the ten forces. This we will discuss in two sections: an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of knowing what is actual, and what is not; followed by an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of knowing the paths that lead to every different kind of goal. Here is the first. 1) The force of knowing what is actual, and what is not [afterword.31] Sanskrit unavailable

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: an explanation of the five forces beginning with that of understanding the paths that lead to every different kind of goal. 6) The force of understanding the paths that lead to different goals [afterword.36] Sanskrit unavailable

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, DE LAS LDOG PAR ZHES SOGS TSIGS BCAD GCIG GIS STON LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, de las ldog par zhes sogs tshigs bcad gcig gis ston la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above: our assertion that-since the opposite position would be mistaken-we would then fall into the position that things lasted forever, or simply discontinued. This is expressed in the one verse which includes "the opposite of that."

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, KHYOD KYI SMRA BA ZHES SOGS TSIGS BCAD GCIG GIS STON LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, khyod kyi smra ba zhes sogs tshigs bcad gcig gis ston la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: how we can gain a feeling of certainty about other teachings, by extrapolating from this teaching on dependent events. This point is made in the one verse which includes "you are an instructor who..."

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DRI BA DANG DE'I LAN JI LTAR MDZAD PA'I TSUL LO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, dri ba dang de'i lan ji ltar mdzad pa'i tshul lo
object.english: Here is our second point from above: the way in which the questioning and answering proceeded. We will describe separately how each of these was accomplished.

object.acip: GNYIS PA DE LA BRTEN NAS JI LTAR 'TSANG RGYA BA'I TSUL LA GNYIS GYI DANG PO NUS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa de la brten nas ji ltar 'tshang rgya ba'i tshul la gnyis gyi dang po nus pa ni
object.english: Here is our second point from above, about how it is that we reach enlightenment by utilizing these paths. We proceed in two steps, the first being a statement that it is surely possible.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, GSUNG RAB KUN GYI SNYING PO SOGS BZHI STE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gsung rab kun gyi snying po sogs bzhi ste
object.english: Our second point here-the benefits we receive from putting things into actual practice this way-is presented in the four lines [of Tibetan] which include "the deepest heart of all the high speech of the Enlightened Ones."

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, DAL 'BYOR LA SNYING PO LEN PAR BSKUL BA DANG, SNYING PO JI LTAR LEN TSUL LO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, dal 'byor la snying po len par bskul ba dang, snying po ji ltar len tshul lo
object.english: This brings us to our second point here-the actual instruction. Here we have two parts: strong advice that we try to get the very essence out of the leisure & fortune that we have; and then a description of just how we derive this essence.

object.acip: GNYIS PA SNYING PO JI LTAR LEN TSUL LA GNYIS, LAM GYI DBANG DU BYAS PA'I GSUNG RAB RNAMS 'DU TSUL DANG, NYAMS SU LEN TSUL DNGOS SO, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa snying po ji ltar len tshul la gnyis, lam gyi dbang du byas pa'i gsung rab rnams 'du tshul dang, nyams su len tshul dngos so, ,dang po ni
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from above-a description of just how we derive the essence out of the leisure & fortune that we have. Here we have two topics: how we group the high teachings with regard to the path; and then the actual way in which we go about deriving the essence mentioned. We begin with the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, 'KHOR BAR GANG GIS SOGS TE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, 'khor bar gang gis sogs te
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: the contemplation of the problems of this cycle, in the form of the source of the suffering. This is expressed in the lines that include "what it is that keeps us chained to this cycle of pain":

object.acip: GNYIS PA DE BSGOM PA NI, DE LTAR SHES NAS SOGS TE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa de bsgom pa ni, de ltar shes nas sogs te
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here, on how to keep our patience. This is found in the words of the root text which include "Once they realized this":

object.acip: GNYIS PA BSGOM TSUL NI, DE LTAR SHES NAS SOGS TE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa bsgom tshul ni, de ltar shes nas sogs te
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: how to meditate. This topic is covered in the lines that include "armed with this understanding":

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, DE LTAR SHES NAS SOGS TE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, de ltar shes nas sogs te
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here, on how to perform this meditation on wisdom. This is covered in the wording of the root text which includes "once they understand all this":

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS LAS, ZHI LHAG ZUNG 'BRAL {%'BREL} BSGOM PA'I DGOS PA DANG, BSGOM TSUL DNGOS SO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis las, zhi lhag zung 'bral bsgom pa'i dgos pa dang, bsgom tshul dngos so
object.english: With this, we have reached our second point here-how to combine quietude & special insight into a single unit. We'll present this topic in two parts: an explanation of why we need to meditate upon quietude and special insight combined into a single unit; and then the actual instructions for this particular type of meditation.

object.acip: GNYIS PA, MED LTA DGAG PA BSHAD ZIN DRAN PA LA SBYAR BA DANG, YOD LTA DGAG PA LA MNYAN PAR GDAMS PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa, med lta dgag pa bshad zin dran pa la sbyar ba dang, yod lta dgag pa la mnyan par gdams pa'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: advice that we rely on an understanding of the profound. We'll cover this in two points-helping the reader recall the way in which the extreme view that nothing exists at all has already been refuted; and then advice that we should listen now to how the extreme view that everything exists as it seems is in its turn refuted. Recalling how Lord Buddha has already refuted the idea that nothing exists

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: demonstrating that-when a person comes to a realization where there is no longer any such discrepancy between what they see and what's really there-they can then reach liberation.

object.acip: GNYIS PA GZHAN GYI {%GYI LUGS} LA MYANG 'DAS 'THOB PA MI 'THAD PA LA, MDOR BSTAN PA DANG, RGYAS BSHAD DO, ,DANG PO NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa gzhan gyi la myang 'das 'thob pa mi 'thad pa la, mdor bstan pa dang, rgyas bshad do, ,dang po ni
object.english: With this, we have reached our second point from above, which is why achieving nirvana the way that others describe it must be incorrect. We will cover this point in a summary presentation, and then an expanded explanation. Here is the first.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA, LHAG BCAS MI 'THAD PA DANG, LHAG MED MI 'THAD PA GNYIS,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la, lhag bcas mi 'thad pa dang, lhag med mi 'thad pa gnyis
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, which is a more expanded explanation of why achieving nirvana the way that those others describe it must be incorrect. We cover this in two parts: explaining why their description of nirvana where something is still left over is incorrect; and then explaining why their description of nirvana where nothing is left over is incorrect.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: With this we have reached our second point: denying the extreme of ending-

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA DNGOS DANG PHAN YON NO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la dngos dang phan yon no
object.english: With this, we have reached our second point here: how to reach the realization that things have no nature of their own, by using starting & ending. We will proceed in two steps: the actual presentation, and then the benefits of this particular methodology.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni
object.english: This then brings us to our second point here: the scriptural support.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point from before, on a description of the actual problems of attachment to the parts of a person.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA MDOR BSTAN, RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA, DON BSDU BA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la mdor bstan, rgyas par bshad pa, don bsdu ba'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, where we begin the actual text which the author has committed to compose. We'll cover this in three broad sections: a brief introduction; an extensive explanation; and then a summary.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA MED LTA 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA BSHAD ZIN DRAN PA LA SBYOR BA, YOD LTA 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA MNYAN PAR GDAMS PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la med lta 'gog pa'i rigs pa bshad zin dran pa la sbyor ba, yod lta 'gog pa'i rigs pa mnyan par gdams pa'o
object.english: With this we have reached our second point from above, which is advice to listen to teachings on the profound. We'll present this in two sections: (1) reminding our reader of the process of reasoning, which we've already presented, for denying the view that nothing exists; and then (2) presenting our advice to listen to the reasoning we use to deny the view that everything exists the way it seems to.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, ZHIG SOGS GCIG LA
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, zhig sogs gcig la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point here: how it would also have to be incorrect to say that someone had reached the knowledge of the end. This idea is covered in the single line [of the Tibetan, two lines of the English] of this verse which mention "destroyed."

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, GANG SOGS GNYIS LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gang sogs gnyis la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point, refuting the idea of a nirvana where nothing is left over. This we find in the two lines [four in the English] which mention "when" at this point.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA 'GAG PA RDZAS GRUB DGAG ,SGYU MA LTA BU'I 'GOG PA SGRUB PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la 'gag pa rdzas grub dgag ,sgyu ma lta bu'i 'gog pa sgrub pa'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point in this discussion on nirvana, which is showing how our own position on the question is correct. Here we proceed in two steps of (1) denying that there could be such a thing as a cessation which existed in a substantial way; and (2) proving the idea of a cessation that is similar to a magical illusion.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, SO SO SOGS BZHI LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, so so sogs bzhi la
object.english: Which brings us to our second point, the problems of failing to realize that things have no nature of their own. This is covered in the next verse of the root text; the one which includes the words "individual, ordinary"-

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, RANG RGYUD 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA DANG, RIGS PA DE PHA ROL POS KYANG DON GYIS KHAS BLANGS TSUL DANG, SKYON BRJOD DE RANG GI SBYOR BA LA MI MTSUNGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN NO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gsum, rang rgyud 'gog pa'i rigs pa dang, rigs pa de pha rol pos kyang don gyis khas blangs tshul dang, skyon brjod de rang gi sbyor ba la mi mtshungs pa'i rgyu mtshan no
object.english: Our second point is divided into three parts: reasoning which denies the idea of an independently effective reason; a description of how this reasoning is, implicitly, already accepted by the opponent; and an explanation of why these same criticisms do not apply to our own logic. Why the qualifier "ultimately" was meaningless

object.acip: GNYIS PA SPYOD RGYUD KYI LAM BGROD TSUL LA BZHI, SNOD RUNG DU BYA BA DANG , DAM TSIG DANG SDOM PA DAG PAR BYA BA DANG , BSNYEN PA JI LTAR BYA BA DANG , DNGOS GRUB JI LTAR SGRUB PA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa spyod rgyud kyi lam bgrod tshul la bzhi, snod rung du bya ba dang , dam tshig dang sdom pa dag par bya ba dang , bsnyen pa ji ltar bya ba dang , dngos grub ji ltar sgrub pa'o
object.english: Here next is our second point from above: how we travel the path of secret teachings of the activity class.  Here in this explanation we repeat the same four divisions of (1) how we are made into a worthy vessel; (2) keeping our pledges and commitments purely; (3) how we do our actual practice; and (4) how we reach high spiritual attainments.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, RIM LNGA'I GRANGS DANG GO RIM NGES PA DANG , SO SO'I DON NO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, rim lnga'i grangs dang go rim nges pa dang , so so'i don no
object.english: Here then is our second point, a description of the various divisions of the stage of completion.  We proceed in two steps: an explanation of how the number, and the order, of the five stages is fixed; and then a description of what each stage involves.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, LUGS 'DI'I RNAL 'BYOR PAS SNYING GA'I SNA RTZER SNGAGS KYI THIG LE BSGOMS PAS STENG 'OG GI RLUNG RNAMS SNYING GA'I DH'U T'I'I NANG DU ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I SNANG BA'I YE SHES SKYES PA NAS BSGOMS STOBS KYIS SNYING GA'I RTZA MDUD RDZOGS PAR GROL DE RLUNG SNYING GA'I MI SHIGS PA LA ZHUGS GNAS THIM GSUM BYAS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I SNANG BA'I YE SHES MA SKYES PA'I GNAS SKABS KYI RDZOGS RIM NI, 'PHAGS LUGS KYI RDZOGS RIM LA RIM PA DRUG TU BYAS PA'I RIM PA GNYIS PA'I NGO BO'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, lugs 'di'i rnal 'byor pas snying ga'i sna rtser sngags kyi thig le bsgoms pas steng 'og gi rlung rnams snying ga'i dhU tI'i nang du zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa las byung ba'i snang ba'i ye shes skyes pa nas bsgoms stobs kyis snying ga'i rtsa mdud rdzogs par grol de rlung snying ga'i mi shigs pa la zhugs gnas thim gsum byas pa las byung ba'i snang ba'i ye shes ma skyes pa'i gnas skabs kyi rdzogs rim ni, 'phags lugs kyi rdzogs rim la rim pa drug tu byas pa'i rim pa gnyis pa'i ngo bo'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above--a description of transcendent speech.  Here now is the essential nature of the second stage within the stage of completion, according to the system of the realized being Nagarjuna, and assuming we are talking about the division of this system into six stages: The second stage begins when a deep practitioner of this system uses meditation upon sacred syllables within a drop at the opening of the channel at the heart to bring the upper and lower winds to enter, stay, and dissolve inside the channel of dance--thus giving birth to the wisdom of light.  And this stage continues up to the point where the practitioner is able to use their meditation to release the knot at the heart completely, thus giving rise to the wisdom of light which comes when the inner winds enter, stay, and dissolve into the indestructible drop at the heart.

object.acip: GNYIS PA NI, SPYIR NA BDAG CAG GI STON PAS, DMAN PA LA MOS PA THEG DMAN PA RNAMS LA CHAGS BRAL GYI SPYOD PA DANG , RGYA CHEN PO LA MOS PA PHAR PHYIN THEG PA PA BA RNAMS LA SA DANG PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I SPYOD PA DANG , ZAB MO LA LHAG PAR MOS PA GSANG SNGAGS RGYUD SDE BZHI'I GDUL BYA RNAMS LA 'DOD CHAGS KYI CHOS KYI SPYOD PA STE, SPYOD PA GSUM BSTAN PA LAS, SKABS 'DI'I SPYOD PA NI 'DOD CHAGS KYI SPYOD PA YIN LA,
object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, spyir na bdag cag gi ston pas, dman pa la mos pa theg dman pa rnams la chags bral gyi spyod pa dang , rgya chen po la mos pa phar phyin theg pa pa ba rnams la sa dang pha rol tu phyin pa'i spyod pa dang , zab mo la lhag par mos pa gsang sngags rgyud sde bzhi'i gdul bya rnams la 'dod chags kyi chos kyi spyod pa ste, spyod pa gsum bstan pa las, skabs 'di'i spyod pa ni 'dod chags kyi spyod pa yin la
object.english: This brings us then to our second point.  Generally speaking, our Teacher has taught three different modes of activity.  He taught the mode of activity which is free of desire to those of the lower way: to those who are attracted to something lower.  He then taught the mode of activity of the bodhisattva paths, and the perfections, to those of the way of the perfections: to those who are attracted to what is far-reaching.  And then He taught the mode of activity which utilizes desire to those of the four classes of the way of the secret word: to those who are deeply attracted to what is deep.  Of these three different modes of activity, the one we are talking about here is that where we utilize desire.

object.acip: GNYIS PA LA GNYIS, GANG LA GNAD DU BSNUN PAR BYA BA RDO RJE'I LUS DANG , DE LA GNAD DU BSNUN PAR BYED PA SBYOR BA YAN LAG DRUG GO
object.wylie: gnyis pa la gnyis, gang la gnad du bsnun par bya ba rdo rje'i lus dang , de la gnad du bsnun par byed pa sbyor ba yan lag drug go
object.english: This brings us to our second point: how we practice the stage of completion in the Wheel of Time.  Here we will describe the diamond body--that is, where it is that we work on the critical points; and the six-part practice of the inner winds, which is what we use to work at these critical points.

object.acip: GNYIS PA RIGS NI, YUL DE NA MI RIGS MI GCIG PA, RGYAL RIGS DANG , RJE RIGS DANG , BRAM ZE'I RIGS DANG , DMANGS RIGS DANG , GDOL PA'I RIGS LA SOGS TE MI 'DRA BA DU MA YOD PA'I NANG NAS MCHOG TU GYUR SHING SA LA LTA BU, RIGS CHE SHING BRTZUN PA, SH'AKYA'I RIGS KYI RGYAL RGYUD DU SKU KHRUNGS,
object.wylie: gnyis pa rigs ni, yul de na mi rigs mi gcig pa, rgyal rigs dang , rje rigs dang , bram ze'i rigs dang , dmangs rigs dang , gdol pa'i rigs la sogs te mi 'dra ba du ma yod pa'i nang nas mchog tu gyur shing sa la lta bu, rigs che shing brtsun pa, shAkya'i rigs kyi rgyal rgyud du sku khrungs
object.english: Which brings us to our second point, His ancestral lineage.  This land in which Naropa took His holy birth was split up into different levels of society, with a great many different castes such as the royalty; the nobility; the priests; the common people; and the outcastes--people like the butchers. Among all these different groups, there was one mighty and upright clan which stood out as supreme--a people like the sal tree, with its wood of natural white incense.  This was the Shakya clan, and Naropa was born into a royal lineage within this very people.

object.acip: GNYIS PA THUN MONG MIN PA'I SNGON 'GRO NI, THUN MONG MIN PA'I BLA MA'I RNAL 'BYOR GYI 'KHRID CES GSUNGS PA 'DI LA BZHI,

object.wylie: spyod bsdus las kyang, rdo rje dang padma mnyam par sbyor ba med par rnam par shes pa gsum nye bar mtshon par mi nus so, ,bha ga dang ling ga yang dag par sbyor bar mi nus pa des ni bde ba chen po'i ting nge 'dzin mi rnyed do, ,ces gsungs pa'i phyir
object.english: And its truth is also demonstrated by the Summary of Activities [a classical tantra on the five stages]: Unless the diamond and the lotus are joined together, there is no way that we can replicate these three states of mind. This was composed by the great Mongol savant Chuje Ngawang Pelden (b. 1797). object.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gtsang sbra gsum byas pa las byung ba'i bsod nams su gang gyur ba, sgrub pa po'i yon tan rgya chen po ni smra bar nus par 'os pa ma yin no
object.english: Here is our second point from above.  The amount of merit produced by performing the practice of the three purities--the vast good qualities of a person who undertakes such a practice--are not something that could ever properly be expressed.

object.acip: GNYIS PA 'GYUR PHYAG NI, MDO SNGAGS KYI CHOS BSTAN PA'I (BKA' DRIN) DANG (MNYAM) PA GZHAN (MED) PA'I (BLA MA) STE GONG MA'AM LHAG MA (DAM PA) STE MCHOG (RNAMS KYI ZHABS LA PHYAG 'TSAL ZHING SKYABS SU MCHI'O,),
object.wylie: gnyis pa 'gyur phyag ni, mdo sngags kyi chos bstan pa'i (bka' drin) dang (mnyam) pa gzhan (med) pa'i (bla ma) ste gong ma'am lhag ma (dam pa) ste mchog (rnams kyi zhabs la phyag 'tshal zhing skyabs su mchi'o,)
object.english: This brings us to our second point--the translator's obeisance.  The text begins now with I bow to the blessed feet of my "holy"--which here means "supreme"--Lamas, who are matchless in Their kindness.  This kindness consists of the fact that they have granted to us the Dharma of both the open and secret teachings.  Remember that the word lama itself means higher, or beyond.  And I come to my Lamas for shelter.

object.acip: GNYIS PA 'KHOR BSKYED TSUL NI, MTHA' SKOR RIM BZHIN, ZHES PA NAS, RDO RJE GSUM MTSAN ZHES PA'I BAR RKANG PA PHYED DANG GSUM STE, KHROM 'TSOGS MTHO BRTZEGS GNYIS LAS 'DIR KHROM 'TSOGS YIN PAS,
object.wylie: gnyis pa 'khor bskyed tshul ni, mtha' skor rim bzhin, zhes pa nas, rdo rje gsum mtshan zhes pa'i bar rkang pa phyed dang gsum ste, khrom 'tshogs mtho brtsegs gnyis las 'dir khrom 'tshogs yin pas
object.english: [27 continued...] This brings us to our second point from above, on how we bring forth our Lama's retinue.  This is presented in the four and a half lines of the translation which begin with "Surrounding Him are rows..." and continue up to "...the three doors of expression."  There are two traditional ways of visualizing this retinue--in a crowd as you might see in an open market; and in groups like terraces.  What we use here is the former.

object.acip: GNYIS PA MCHOD PA 'BUL BA NI PHYAG BYA BA'I YAN LAG ZIN PA DE (NAS MCHOD PA'I YAN LAG NI, MCHOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM) STE MCHOD PA DANG, MCHOD YUL DANG, MCHOD MKHAN GSUM (PO RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA BDE STONG DBYER MED) KYIS (RGYAS BTAB NAS 'BUL BA) YIN LA, BDE STONG GI DON RGYAS PAR NI BLA MA'I MAN NGAG LAS BTZAL DGOS SO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa mchod pa 'bul ba ni phyag bya ba'i yan lag zin pa de (nas mchod pa'i yan lag ni, mchod pa'i 'khor gsum) ste mchod pa dang, mchod yul dang, mchod mkhan gsum (po rnam par mi rtog pa bde stong dbyer med) kyis (rgyas btab nas 'bul ba) yin la, bde stong gi don rgyas par ni bla ma'i man ngag las btsal dgos so
object.english: This brings us to our second point, the presentation of offerings.  Now that the step of bowing is completed, the next step is to present Them with offerings.  We make our presentation then as follows, being sure to stamp the practice with our realization that the three elements of the act of giving--the gift, the one receiving the gift, and the giver--are indivisible bliss and voidness, beyond all conception.  Those of you who would like to understand this idea of bliss and voidness in greater detail should seek private instructions from your Lama on the matter.

object.acip: GNYIS PA DE NYID RAB DBYE'I SGO NAS RGYAS PAR BSHAD PA LA LNGA, PHYI DANG, NANG DANG, GSANG BA, DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA, SMAN DANG LUS 'BUL BA'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa de nyid rab dbye'i sgo nas rgyas par bshad pa la lnga, phyi dang, nang dang, gsang ba, de kho na nyid kyi mchod pa, sman dang lus 'bul ba'o
object.english: This brings us to our second point: a more expanded explanation of the different types of offering.  We proceed through five subjects--the outer offering, the inner offering, the secret offering, the offering of suchness, and the offering of both the elixir and our own body.

object.acip: GNYIS PA GANG LA JI LTAR 'BUL BA NI, (DANG BA) STE DAD PA('I SEMS KYIS PHUL DU BYUNG) BA'I MCHOD YUL (ZHING GI MCHOG) SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI (SKYABS MGON THUGS RJE'I GTER) MDZOD DU GYUR PA'I BLA MA 'KHOR DANG BCAS PA RNAMS (LA DBUL BAR BGYI)'O,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa gang la ji ltar 'bul ba ni, (dang ba) ste dad pa('i sems kyis phul du byung) ba'i mchod yul (zhing gi mchog) sngar bshad pa ltar gyi (skyabs mgon thugs rje'i gter) mdzod du gyur pa'i bla ma 'khor dang bcas pa rnams (la dbul bar bgyi)'o
object.english: This brings us then to our second point: how we present our offering, and to whom.  I offer all these to that highest karmic object, to the most excellent object of any offering: to my Lama (along with those in His circle), who--as we mentioned before--is a treasure house, a massive storehouse of compassion, my Savior and Protector.  And I do so with thoughts of faith and devotion. The Offering of Our Practice

object.acip: GNYIS PA ZHAR BYUNG RGYA JA'I MCHOD PA NI, GUR GUM MDANGS LDAN SOGS RKANG PA GNYIS TE (GUR GUM) GYI (MDANGS) MDOG LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR SER DANG (LDAN) ZHING (BZANG PO) SHIN TU DRI ZHIM PO'I DRI NGAD CAN (RO BRGYA) STE RO BCUD MANG PO DANG LDAN PA'I (DPAL 'DZIN) PA STE YOD PA'I (RGYA JA'I BTUNG BA) RNAMS KYANG 'BUL LO,,
object.wylie: gnyis pa zhar byung rgya ja'i mchod pa ni, gur gum mdangs ldan sogs rkang pa gnyis te (gur gum) gyi (mdangs) mdog lta bu kha dog dmar ser dang (ldan) zhing (bzang po) shin tu dri zhim po'i dri ngad can (ro brgya) ste ro bcud mang po dang ldan pa'i (dpal 'dzin) pa ste yod pa'i (rgya ja'i btung ba) rnams kyang 'bul lo
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above: an incidental offering of fine Chinese tea.  This is presented in the three lines that mention tea "of a saffron hue."  And so here I offer cups of the tea from China which is of the finest sort--which possesses or gives off the finest, most delightful fragrance: a truly delicious scent.  This tea is laden with a thousand flavors, meaning that it has many different tastes at its heart, and has a reddish golden color similar to the hue of saffron.

object.acip: GNYIS PA THAR 'DOD KYI THABS NI, BZOD DKA' SOGS RKANG BA BZHI STE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa thar 'dod kyi thabs ni, bzod dka' sogs rkang ba bzhi ste
object.english: This brings us to our second point from above, on the method to be used by those who seek for freedom.  This is presented in the four lines of the Tibetan which include the word "unbearable."

object.acip: GNYIS PA RKYEN NGAN LAM DU SLONG TSUL NI, SNOD BCUD SOGS RKANG PA BZHI STE,
object.wylie: gnyis pa rkyen ngan lam du slong tshul ni, snod bcud sogs rkang pa bzhi ste
object.english: Next is our second point, the instructions for turning problems into a path.  These are found in the four lines of the Tibetan which talk about "this world and every being who lives in this world."

object.acip: YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA NA RNAG KHRAG MTHONG BA DE YANG YI DVAGS 'GA' ZHIG LA YIN GYI, YI DVAGS THAMS CAD LA MA YIN TE, YI DVAGS LA PHYI'I SGRIB PA CAN, NANG GI SGRIB PA CAN, ZAS SKOM NYID LA YOD PA'I SGRIB PA CAN DU MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa na rnag khrag mthong ba de yang yi dvags 'ga' zhig la yin gyi, yi dvags thams cad la ma yin te, yi dvags la phyi'i sgrib pa can, nang gi sgrib pa can, zas skom nyid la yod pa'i sgrib pa can du ma yod pa'i phyir
object.english: When we say that a craving spirit looks at a stream of water and sees pus and blood, by the way, we are only talking about some kinds of craving spirits, and not all of them. This is because there are many kinds of craving spirits: some with obstacles in the world around them that prevent them from relieving their craving; some with obstacles that are parts of their bodies; and some with obstacles that relate to the food or drink itself.

object.acip: YANG KHA CIG, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES DANG , 'BRAS BU CAN GYI LJON PA LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, 'BRAS BU MED PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I DE'I MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PAR THAL, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, RNAG KHRAG DNGOS GNAS PA LA TSAD MAR SONG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES TSAD MA YOD PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: yang kha cig, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe, chu klung bskams pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes dang , 'bras bu can gyi ljon pa la bltas pa de'i tshe, 'bras bu med pa la tshad mar song ba'i de'i mig shes tshad ma yod par thal, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la bltas pa de'i tshe, rnag khrag dngos gnas pa la tshad mar song ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes tshad ma yod pa'i phyir
object.english: Yet again, another argument might be made: Let's take the case of one of those craving spirits that looks at a river of water, and sees it as a dry riverbed, genuinely so. Or consider one that looks at a tree loaded with fruit, but sees it as nothing but bare limbs, genuinely so. The visual consciousness of both of these beings then must be a valid perception. Why? Remember the case of the three different beings looking at a glass full of something wet and flowing; according to you, the pus and blood was actual pus and blood, and the perception of them by the craving spirit was genuine: his visual consciousness was a valid perception.

object.acip: RNAM PA GCIG TU NA, YI DVAGS KYIS CHU KLUNG LA BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA DE MA BSKAMS KYANG , RANG GI BLTA BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG DANG , LONGS SPYOD BYAR GYUR PA'I CHU KLUNG BSKAMS PA YOD DE, 'GRO BA GSUM GYIS BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA PHOR PA GANG LA CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE NA, LAS KYI DBANG GIS RNAG KHRAG SOGS DNGOS PO RNAM PA GSUM CIG CAR DU GRUB PA ZHIG YOD PA'I PHYIR,
object.wylie: rnam pa gcig tu na, yi dvags kyis chu klung la bltas pa de'i tshe na de ma bskams kyang , rang gi blta byar gyur pa'i chu klung dang , longs spyod byar gyur pa'i chu klung bskams pa yod de, 'gro ba gsum gyis brlan zhing gsher ba phor pa gang la cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe na, las kyi dbang gis rnag khrag sogs dngos po rnam pa gsum cig car du grub pa zhig yod pa'i phyir
object.english: From one point of view, the river of water hasn't dried up when the craving spirit looks at it; but there is a river which has dried up, if you're talking about a river of water that the spirit can see, or a river of water that the spirit can drink from.
